Chapter I

Plan and Scope of the Work

WHY THE STUDY WAS UNDERTAKEN

The idea of treating the history of Savoy College as a thesis arose after a scattering of ex-students of the College had requested some research work to be done from a file of Bonham newspapers, available then at The University of Texas Library. These ex-students had waited a history written; however, at that time it was desired to have it very brief. The idea grew; interest grew; preliminary research revealed that the College had been unique in several important points, and that in its brief span of fourteen years it had created a definite place in the growth of public education in Texas before the State had made adequate provision for that important branch of formal schooling. This research showed also that the College was not so far removed from reach that much material, enough valuable data were available to make the undertaking worthwhile.

Ever present has been the author's desire to gather and present facts that may aid ex-students to keep their college days in memory and to record for future historians the workings of an able and much-loved educator—Professor R. R. Halsell—and his noteworthy pioneering school.

SOURCES OF INFORMATION

The richest source of material for this history has been found in the ex-students themselves. Between twenty-five and forty-five letters, representing correspondence with about forty different students (together with more than forty-five personal interviews), have been most helpful in the endeavor to gather data of the College as it was more than fifty years ago.
